questions.title: Does arm posture affect object selection?
questions.question: Can the same new instruction select a different object when the arm starts from a different pose?
questions.design: DM0.5, Object soup → cream cheese, five pre-contact states. Compare original vs revised instructions within each posture. Neutral preparation repositions the arm for 60 controller actions while preserving the object layout.
questions.watch: Watch the first contacted object, then the final placement. Selecting the new object is different from successfully placing it.
questions.limit: A small engineering diagnostic, not a full-suite score. It does not isolate visual observations from proprioception or identify an internal mechanism.

questions.title: Does changing the instruction redirect the continuation?
questions.question: From a saved state, what changes when the policy receives the original, revised, or suffix-only instruction?
questions.design: Matched-state 300-action and 600-action studies, plus Light-WAM and CAG-VA comparisons. Use the same study, state, phase, and horizon when comparing branches.
questions.watch: Compare first contacts and original/revised goal timelines. A revised goal can become true while obsolete behavior continues.
questions.limit: Action similarity alone does not establish that language is ignored. Different models and horizons are separate diagnostic conditions, not independent repetitions of one experiment.

questions.title: Does explicit replacement—or simply waiting—help?
questions.question: Does saying not to pick the old object change selection? Does a duration-matched hold have the same effect as repositioning?
questions.design: DM0.5 Object revisions compare ordinary revised wording with explicit replacement or a hold before continuation. Preparation duration is shown separately.
questions.watch: Look for the first object contact. A hold controls for elapsed time; it is not identical to moving the arm.
questions.limit: These are wording and preparation controls. The two post-preparation physical states must not be described as identical.

questions.title: Is changing the object different from changing its destination?
questions.question: Can the policy redirect A → P to A → Q as readily as it can switch to B → P?
questions.design: PI0/PI0.5 GOAL and legacy PI0 Spatial comparisons use original continuations as controls. Select the same model, initial state, and phase to compare revision types.
questions.watch: Destination revisions can reuse the original object. Object revisions require reselecting a different object. Check their distinct goal rows.
questions.limit: Geometry and intervention-state feasibility can differ. This comparison alone does not establish that one semantic type is inherently harder.

questions.title: Does the robot follow a changed execution order?
questions.question: If soup-then-tomato changes to tomato-then-soup, does the sequence actually change?
questions.design: PI0 Long, five states. Compare forward-order and reverse-order instructions from the same pre-contact boundary, with 550 continuation actions.
questions.watch: Read the requested-order row, not only the full-goal row. Both objects can end in the basket even when the requested order is violated.
questions.limit: Final object positions cannot establish temporal order. These engineering comparisons are separate from the formal benchmark.

questions.title: Does behavior change with wording, scene, or layout?
questions.question: After soup is already in the basket, does the robot place tomato or the newly requested cheese?
questions.design: OpenVLA-OFT Long state0. Same-L0-state wording comparisons are distinct from official-L7-scene and object-layout interventions.
questions.watch: Compare tomato placement, cheese placement, and preservation of soup. Scene/layout videos intentionally change physical configuration.
questions.limit: One-state probes show scene/layout sensitivity in these examples. They do not identify a general causal mechanism; scene controls are not same-state comparisons.

questions.title: Can a non-policy controller complete the goal?
questions.question: Is there an independent physical witness of goal feasibility at the intervention state?
questions.design: Original-policy continuations are displayed beside separately labeled reference-controller continuations.
questions.watch: The right branch is not a VLA. Its success can demonstrate a feasible trajectory, not policy adaptation.
questions.limit: Reference failure does not prove physical impossibility. A successful reference is not counted as VLA success.

questions.title: Does a stop request stop obsolete behavior?
questions.question: What happens when the task is cancelled without a replacement goal?
questions.design: PI0 GOAL: original continuation versus a prompt-only stop request from matched boundaries.
questions.watch: Inspect residual motion, continued task execution, and object handling. Completing the original goal is not cancellation success.
questions.limit: No overall safe-stop score is assigned: stopping and release thresholds have not been frozen.
